newsitem.title: USA: MedCath to open 20 heart hospitals.
newsitem.headline: MedCath to open 20 heart hospitals.

text.p: MedCath Inc. said Wednesday the company plans to soon open cardiac care hospitals in 20 states that have expanded the market for such services.
MedCath, based in Charlotte, N.C., provides cardiology and cardiovascular services through the development, operation and management of such hospitals.
Federal law had limited the market for such services, but regulators in 20 states have now dropped the so-called "certificate of need" in order to allow competition.
"We're targeting all 20 states," Chairman Stephen Puckett said during MedCath's annual meeting here.
MedCath, which also manages the practices of 76 physicians, opened its first heart hospital in McAllen, Texas, last year.
Last week, it opened another in Little Rock, Ark. Others are planned in Tucson, Ariz., in October; Austin, Texas in spring of 1998 and Bakersfield, Calif., in fall of 1998.
Puckett said he expects competition to increase as more states deregulate.
"The states that have dropped their (certificate of need) are mostly in the West," he said, but Indiana, Ohio and Pennsylvania have also taken the step.
MedCath also has a diagnostics unit that supplements hospital services via mobile laboratories.
MedCath stock rose 25 cents to $15.25 on Nasdaq in early afternoon trading.
